decision.title: Type registry and sequence types
decision.summary: sxml_type_identifier names schema and item types in one space, with built-ins as constants below 70, interned item types from 512, and sequence types as the plain value sxml_sequence_type.

body.p: (task 0.7). sxml_type_identifier (32-bit index) names every type: schema types and item types share one space, since atomic types are both (XDM 4.0, section 4.1.2). Built-in types (all XSD/XDM built-ins including xs:untyped, xs:numeric, xs:error, the list types, and the generic item types item(), node(), element(), function(*), map(*), array(*), record(*), ...) have constant identifiers SXML_TYPE_* below 70, described by static const data; the enum only grows. Identifiers 70-511 are reserved for later built-ins; registered types start at 512. Item types written in queries (node tests, function, map, array, record, enumeration, choice and JNode types) are registered and interned, so structural equality is identifier equality; nominative record types are declared, then defined, so they can be recursive. Schema types (Phase 5) are registered into the same table. A sequence type is not registered: it is the plain value sxml_sequence_type (item type + occurrence), with occurrences as bit sets so occurrence subtyping is a subset test. Predicates (, is_subtype) return bool and treat unknown identifiers as false.
